title: Proof on the Page
description: Audit visible trust evidence across an online store and turn the gaps into a practical plan for product pages.

sections.heading: Audit sixteen evidence signals
sections.body: Review the home, About, product, returns and contact pages for evidence of experience, expertise, authority and trust using the workbook’s own scoring rubric.

sections.heading: Make proof useful at the point of decision
sections.body: Work through founder-story fields, genuine review prompts and product-knowledge checks. Map where certifications, reviews, warranties and other evidence support a shopper’s decision.

sections.heading: Build a thirty-day action plan
sections.body: Prioritize gaps by impact, effort and ownership. Use the weekly plan and one-page proof template to document actions and reassess visible evidence.

methodology: Choose representative store pages, record evidence for each of the sixteen signals, and use the proof-placement matrix to prioritize changes. Validate product facts and obtain permission for names and customer photos.
limitations: The sixteen-signal score is an author-created audit aid, not a Google E-E-A-T score or confirmed ranking formula. Evidence visibility does not establish causation, and collapsed content is not necessarily inaccessible to search engines.
